content.user_title: Verify Rust Proofs and SMT Queries with Sail
content.value_statement: Repeated verification can delay Rust proof development and leave agents working with outdated evidence. This skill guides Sail verification, proof repair checks, and cached SMT queries with explicit result interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Guide Cargo and Verus project verification using Sail and compatible verification arguments.
Explain proof repair validation that checks a selected function before requiring whole-target verification.
Describe background verification jobs and result retrieval through CLI commands or configured MCP tools.
Guide complete SMT-LIB transcript submission to bundled Z3 and interpretation of outcomes, models, and cache hits.
Distinguish evidence freshness from verification success and identify partial verification scope.
Explain release-dependent standalone Rust verification and installed capability checks.
limitations: Sail supports Linux x86-64 and Apple-silicon macOS; this skill does not provide the required binaries.
Standalone Rust file verification requires a supporting build; the reference excludes published Sail 0.1.0.
Proof repair validation requires the interactive engine in the same Sail cache; MCP workflows require a configured server.
An SMT answer covers its submitted formula, and a selected function passing does not establish whole-target verification.

use_cases.title: Iterate on Rust proofs
use_cases.description: Run Sail verification after proof edits, inspect failure diagnostics, and preserve intended contracts while checking current whole-target results.

use_cases.title: Validate agent-generated repairs
use_cases.description: Check candidate repairs through CLI or MCP workflows and accept them only after completed whole-target verification.

use_cases.title: Repeat solver experiments
use_cases.description: Submit complete SMT-LIB transcripts, inspect satisfiability and models, and recognize reuse of matching decided requests.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use sail-verification to check this Cargo and Verus project. Report the verdict, checked scope, and evidence freshness.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect an existing proof workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a proof failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Verus failure with Sail. Propose a repair that preserves the intended contract, then reverify and report remaining failures.

prompt_templates.title: Run a cached SMT query
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Sail runtime capabilities, then run my complete SMT-LIB transcript. Report outcomes, requested models or cores, and cache reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a repair through MCP
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configured Sail MCP server to validate this candidate proof repair. Inspect tool schemas, track completion, and require current whole-target success.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: supervise asynchronous proof repair validation.

output_examples.input: Explain the documented SMT example that constrains an integer count to exceed two.
output: A returned model assigns count an integer greater than two.
An identical decided request can reuse cached output; inspect the reported cache hit.
This result concerns the submitted formula, not a Rust implementation.

output_examples.input: A selected function passed, but the evidence is Historical. Can I report that the project verifies?
output: No. A selected function result does not establish whole-target success.
Historical evidence no longer matches the present inputs.
Run verification again and check both the currentness and verdict for the intended target.

best_practices: Inspect installed CLI help and MCP tool schemas before selecting release-dependent workflows or arguments.
Preserve intended contracts and check both whole-target scope and current evidence after edits.
Keep transcripts, logs, and redirected output outside watched project inputs to avoid invalidating freshness.
anti_patterns: Weakening specifications solely to make a failing implementation verify.
Reporting historical evidence, readiness checks, or partial verification as current whole-target success.
Treating unknown answers, timeouts, or incomplete executions as successful solver evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill install Sail or its solvers?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and installation references. Sail supplies its own Verus and Z3 runtimes.

faq.question: Which operating systems does Sail support?
faq.answer: The skill documents Linux x86-64 and Apple-silicon macOS.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill targets all three tools. CLI workflows require Sail, while MCP workflows require a configured Sail server.

faq.question: Can every Sail 0.1.0 build verify standalone Rust files?
faq.answer: No. The reference excludes published 0.1.0 and notes development builds can share that version. Inspect installed help for standalone support.

faq.question: Does Current evidence mean verification succeeded?
faq.answer: No. Current describes freshness. Read the verdict and checked scope separately, and verify again after further edits.

faq.question: When does Sail reuse an SMT result?
faq.answer: Reuse requires matching script bytes, limits, pinned solver identity, and execution settings. Unknown answers, timeouts, and incomplete executions are not cached as successful evidence.
